content.key_idea: Ramps (early exits) can only be injected where a layer's intermediate output represents the full extent of data flow at that point, so feasible ramp locations differ across ResNet, VGG and BERT block structures.

evidence: Apparate only injects ramps that make full use of available data flows at that part of the model.
for VGG models, ramps are feasible at all layers since their intermediates represent the full extent

summary: Apparate automatically injects and manages early exits (ramps) in ML models. Figure 7 illustrates where ramps can feasibly be placed for three different model architectures. Panel (a) shows a ResNet block (Input, Weight Layer, ReLU, Weight Layer, Add, ReLU) with green checks and red X's marking which points along the residual path allow a ramp. Panel (b) shows a VGG stack of Conv/Pooling layers, where ramps are feasible after every layer since each intermediate reflects the full data flow. Panel (c) shows a BERT Encoder block (Multi-Head Attention, Add & Norm, Feed Forward, Add & Norm), where ramps are restricted to block boundaries rather than mid-block, since attention needs complete inputs. The three small, similarly structured diagrams are placed side by side to let a reader compare ramp feasibility across model families at a glance.
summary_zh: 图7比较了在ResNet、VGG和BERT三种模型结构中早退出（ramp）的可行插入位置：绿色对勾表示该处数据流完整、可插入ramp，红叉表示不可行，三个模型的层堆栈并排展示便于对比。
